clue.text: Umbrellas, British, and hand-made cigarettes?

parts.note: rollies is informal British slang for roll-your-own cigarettes

explanation.surface: A list of things someone carries: umbrellas, a British passport perhaps, and some roll-ups.
explanation.walkthrough: BROLLY is everyday British slang for an umbrella; ROLLIES are cigarettes rolled by hand from loose tobacco.
explanation.definitionFit: Brollies is the colloquial British plural for rain shades carried overhead.

clue.text: Old man climbing with little desire

indicators.note: in a down entry, climbing means the letters run upwards, so the word for old man is read backwards

parts.note: PA is an informal word for father, one's old man
petite means small or dainty

explanation.surface: An elderly man going up a slope with hardly any enthusiasm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Climbing' only works as a reversal because this is a down clue: PA read bottom to top gives AP.
explanation.definitionFit: Appetite is a craving or wish for something, a close synonym of desire.

clue.text: Before dance catch game

indicators.note: the word for catch is placed in front of the word for dance

parts.note: to net a fish is to catch it
a ball is a formal dance

explanation.surface: Someone told to catch something before a dance gets going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Before' sets the catch ahead of the dance. Netball is a team sport much played in British schools, akin to basketball.
explanation.definitionFit: Netball is a team sport, so it is an example of a game.

clue.text: Baby in cooler temperature

parts.note: a fan is a device that cools the air

explanation.surface: A baby kept cool when the temperature drops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cooler' looks like an adjective but is a noun: something that cools, a FAN.
explanation.definitionFit: An infant is a very young child, which is what a baby is.

clue.text: Bordeaux and Irish county twinned initially

parts.note: Clare is a county on the west coast of Ireland

indicators.note: initially asks for only the opening letter of the word twinned

explanation.surface: A French wine region and an Irish county linked as twin towns.
explanation.walkthrough: County CLARE is in the west of Ireland; 'initially' takes T from 'twinned'.
explanation.definitionFit: Claret is the traditional British name for red wine from the Bordeaux region.

clue.text: Soldier by airplane ordered to carry hot gear

parts.note: a para is a paratrooper, a soldier

indicators.note: the rearranged letters hold the abbreviation for hot within them, as if carrying it
ordered means arranged afresh, so the letters of airplane are put in a new order

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A paratrooper is told to carry hot equipment onto the plane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ordered' rearranges the plane word to PERNALIA; 'to carry' sets H after its P. 'Airplane' is the American spelling the anagram needs.
explanation.definitionFit: Paraphernalia means miscellaneous equipment or belongings, which is gear in the sense of kit.

clue.text: Not the architectural style associated with Pisa's tower?

definitions.text: Not the architectural style associated with Pisa's tower?

parts.words: Not the architectural style associated with Pisa's tower?
parts.note: names an English Gothic style which also means exactly upright, the one thing the leaning tower is not

explanation.surface: A puzzle about what style of building the Leaning Tower of Pisa is not.
explanation.walkthrough: Perpendicular is the late English Gothic style of church architecture; the word also means exactly vertical, which Pisa's leaning tower famously is not.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both an architectural period and an upright line, and the tilted tower fails the second sense.

clue.text: Drunken pair connected more than usually liable to mishap

definitions.text: more than usually liable to mishap

indicators.note: drunken suggests staggering about, so the letters of pair connected are jumbled

explanation.surface: Two drunks hooked together are more likely than most to come to grief.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone accident-prone tends to have mishaps more often than others.

clue.text: Screen in restaurant close to home

parts.note: a grill is a restaurant serving grilled food

indicators.note: close to means the end of the word, so only the final letter of home is used

explanation.surface: A partition in an eatery not far from where someone lives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Close to' reads as 'near' but means the closing letter of 'home', E.
explanation.definitionFit: A grille is a grating or lattice used as a screen in front of a window or opening.

clue.text: Snake bit, causing famous row

parts.note: a boa is a large constricting snake
a trace is a small amount, a bit

explanation.surface: A snake bite leading to a well-known quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' means rowing a boat, not a quarrel: the Boat Race is the annual Oxford v Cambridge rowing contest on the Thames.
explanation.definitionFit: The Boat Race is the best-known rowing event in Britain, so a famous row.

clue.text: Afternoon meal Athena regularly provides

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of the name Athena, here the second, fourth and sixth

explanation.surface: The goddess Athena reliably serves the afternoon refreshments.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain tea is a light meal of sandwiches and cakes taken in the late afternoon.

clue.text: Twins for example overturned car

indicators.note: overturned means flipped over, so the abbreviation for for example is reversed

parts.note: EG is the abbreviation of exempli gratia, for example
the Mini is a small British car

explanation.surface: A pair of twins, say, flipped their car over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For example' looks like it introduces Twins but supplies EG, which 'overturned' turns to GE.
explanation.definitionFit: Gemini is the zodiac sign of the Twins, Castor and Pollux.

clue.text: Broken tie with adult brings freedom

indicators.note: broken means smashed into pieces, so the letters of tie and adult are reassembled

explanation.surface: Cutting ties as a grown-up gives a person their liberty.
explanation.definitionFit: Latitude is scope or room to act as one pleases, a kind of freedom.

clue.text: Diamonds and cool stuff

definitions.meaning: frozen water is literally cool stuff

explanation.surface: Gems and something chilly side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is slang for gemstones and also the ordinary name for frozen water.

clue.text: Poem unknown about Yankee ship's epic journey

indicators.note: about means going around, so the poem's letters surround the next pieces

parts.note: an ode is a lyric poem
Yankee is Y in the NATO phonetic alphabet
SS stands for steamship, with the apostrophe s as a link
Y is an algebraic unknown, like x

explanation.surface: A poem of uncertain authorship about an American ship's grand voyage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' wraps the poem round Yankee and ship's; the unknown comes last. 'Poem' tempts as the definition, but Homer's title is the answer for the journey.
explanation.definitionFit: Homer's Odyssey tells of a long wandering voyage, so the word now means any epic journey.

clue.text: To spill beans not good, evil

indicators.note: not means the letter for good is left out

parts.note: to sing is slang for informing, spilling the beans

explanation.surface: Telling secrets is wicked, not good at all.
explanation.walkthrough: SING is underworld slang for confessing or informing, which is what spilling the beans means.
explanation.definitionFit: A sin is a wicked act, so evil in the noun sense of wrongdoing.

clue.text: Pleasantly mild Liberal embraced by setter?

indicators.note: embraced by means held inside, so the letter for Liberal goes within the setter word

parts.note: cement is something that sets hard, a setter

explanation.surface: Is the crossword compiler a gentle Liberal at heart?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Setter' looks like the crossword compiler, as often meant by 'setter', but here is a thing that sets: CEMENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Clement weather is mild and agreeable, so the word means pleasantly mild.

clue.text: Underwear has one inside leering, unfortunately

indicators.note: inside means the letter for one is placed within the rearranged letters
unfortunately suggests something gone wrong, so the letters of leering are rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone eyeing up a person's underwear with an unfortunate leer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unfortunately' rearranges LEERING to LNGERIE, and 'inside' puts I after the L.
explanation.definitionFit: Lingerie is women's underwear and nightclothes.

clue.text: Stacks concealing a pig in wood

indicators.note: concealing means hiding something within, so the word for stacks holds the other pieces

parts.note: stacks, as in stacks of time, means many
a hog is a pig

explanation.surface: Piles of logs in a forest with a pig hidden among them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stacks' looks like a noun for piles but stands for MANY ('stacks of' = lots).
explanation.definitionFit: Mahogany is a hard reddish-brown timber prized for furniture.

clue.text: Wholesale brawling man sees

indicators.note: brawling suggests a scuffle, so the letters of man and sees are thrown about

explanation.surface: A man watches a fight on a large scale.
explanation.definitionFit: En masse means all together in a body, which is wholesale in its sense of on a large scale.

clue.text: Food, large amount, seen in Biden's birthplace

parts.note: scran is British slang for food
a ton, as in tons of, is a large amount

explanation.surface: Plenty of food spotted in the town where the US president was born.
explanation.walkthrough: SCRAN is British slang, especially northern, for food.
explanation.definitionFit: Joe Biden was born in Scranton, Pennsylvania, in 1942.

clue.text: Knock at sharp nail

parts.note: a tack is a short sharp nail

explanation.surface: Banging away at a pointed nail with a hammer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knock' looks like a blow but means criticise.
explanation.definitionFit: To knock something is to criticise it harshly, which is to attack it.

clue.text: Absorbent cloth covering right garden tool

indicators.note: covering means wrapping round, so the cloth word holds the letter for right

parts.note: a towel is a cloth for drying

explanation.surface: A towel thrown over a gardening implement.
explanation.definitionFit: A trowel is a small hand tool with a scoop blade used for planting.

clue.text: Mobile phone ringing love: have this in despair?

indicators.note: ringing means encircling, so the shuffled letters surround the letter for love
mobile means free to move, so the letters of phone are moved about

parts.note: O is love, a zero score in tennis

explanation.surface: Phoning a lover who never picks up is a recipe for despair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mobile' makes NHOPE from PHONE; 'ringing' puts O inside it. 'Mobile phone ringing' reads as a call coming in.
explanation.definitionFit: Despair is the state of lacking all expectation, so in despair one has none.

clue.text: Rob shilling from complacent chump

indicators.note: to rob is to take something away, so the letter for shilling is removed

parts.note: smug means self-satisfied, complacent
S is the abbreviation for a shilling, an old British coin

explanation.surface: Stealing a shilling from a smug fool.
explanation.walkthrough: A shilling was a pre-decimal British coin, abbreviated s. 'Rob' could itself be the definition, but it is the instruction to take S away.
explanation.definitionFit: A mug is British slang for a gullible person, a chump.

clue.text: Flood defence breached by god with hammer

indicators.note: breached by means broken into, so the god's name goes inside the word for defence

parts.note: a plea is a defendant's answer to a charge in court
Thor is the Norse god of thunder who wields a hammer

explanation.surface: A flood barrier smashed by a hammer-wielding deity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Defence' looks like a flood barrier but is a legal PLEA.
explanation.definitionFit: A plethora is an excessive amount, a flood of something.

clue.text: Xmas booze g-g-gone astray!

indicators.note: astray means gone off course, so the letters of the stammered word are mixed up

explanation.surface: A stammering drinker realises all the Christmas drink has vanished.
explanation.walkthrough: The stutter supplies the extra Gs the anagram needs.
explanation.definitionFit: Eggnog is a rich drink of eggs, cream and often spirits, traditional at Christmas.

clue.text: Clever stuff investing energy and time in geology?

indicators.note: investing means clothing or enclosing, so energy and time go inside the geology phrase

parts.note: geology is the science of rocks, rock science

explanation.surface: Putting time and energy into studying rocks is clever work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Investing' looks like putting in money, but here means clothing or enclosing: energy and time go inside the geology phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Rocket science is the byword for anything intellectually demanding.
